statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Department of Energy Nuclear Transparency Act
sentences: Mr. Speaker, this is a bipartisan bill to ensure that Congress can provide critical oversight over the Department of Energy's nuclear programs and ensure that DOE maintains the highest safety standards for nuclear power.
Nuclear energy provides reliable, clean power across America.
For example, in the State of Florida, my home State, nuclear energy provides 10 percent of our electricity generation.

The Department of Energy plays a crucial role in safeguarding nuclear power as directed by Congress, and in the Atomic Energy Act, Congress specifically gave DOE the authority to conduct research and development of nuclear reactors.
The development of nuclear reactors for research purposes at DOE is separate and apart from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission's approval process for new reactors for commercial use.
Recently, the Department of Energy has undertaken new efforts to research and fast-track advanced nuclear test reactors.
Done wrong, it could be dangerous and shatter public confidence in nuclear power for a generation.

Mr. Speaker, the Congress, through the Energy and Commerce Committee, sought information from the Department of Energy on their new fast- tracking process, and despite repeated requests for information and clarity on DOE's fast-tracked nuclear reactor efforts, the Department provided Congress with very little information about how the Department will preserve safety and transparency.

Mr. Speaker, Congress and the public needs greater transparency on DOE nuclear reactor research and fast-tracking, particularly as DOE has lost a lot of professional staff and technical expertise over the past year.
Nuclear energy cannot succeed in the United States without public trust in the industry.
With responsible leadership and the right policy support, nuclear energy can safely power the U.S. economy with clean, reliable energy.

statements.where: Press release: Castor Champions Passage of Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act to Shield Neighbors from Higher Electric Bills Tied to Data Centers

statements.where: Floor speech, Congressional Record: Ratepayer Protection Act
sentences: I am proud to lead this bipartisan bill with Congressman Evans to protect my neighbors from unfairly paying for the energy needs of large AI data centers.
Too many are struggling under the weight of soul-crushing energy bills, and it comes at a time especially where everything costs more--your groceries, gas, diesel, healthcare, and housing.
But now there is a new stressor: massive hyperscale data centers are connecting to the grid.

When a data center or other large load comes online, it can trigger massive upgrades--new power plants, transmission lines, local transformers--and typically those costs are passed along to ratepayers, and that is not fair.
Our neighbors should not be stuck paying for the energy infrastructure of the wealthiest countries in the world.
The Ratepayer Protection Act says that the data center pays for its own upgrades, not the rest of us.
These monumental hyperscale data centers can span hundreds of thousands of square feet.
Massive hyperscale data centers can continuously consume over 100 megawatts, with the largest facilities consuming over 650 megawatts.

According to the U.S. Department of Energy, right now data centers consume about 4.4 percent of all electricity in America, but they predict that that will go up to 12 percent of the total electricity consumption in America by just 2028.
Mr. Speaker, hyperscale data centers are being constructed by the wealthiest Big Tech corporations on the planet.
As hardworking Americans are just trying to make ends meet, they shouldn't carry Big Tech's data center load as well.
That is why we hammered out the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act, to ensure that data centers pay the full cost of their energy demand and upgrades.
It says that if a company wants to build a data center, they should pay for the power and grid upgrades they need, not the rest of us.
This bill will require those data centers to cover all the costs.

For example, States can require that data centers are powered by clean energy and don't damage local water supplies.
States can even require that data centers fund weatherization initiatives or deployment of energy-saving batteries, rooftop solar, and heat pumps.
For example, Virginia is requiring data centers to cover new transmission and distribution capacity costs.
Minnesota requires data centers to pay into an energy conservation and weatherization fund to benefit working-class neighbors.
Kansas incentivized data centers to participate in demand response programs to reduce peak demand.
This bill also empowers local communities to make decisions on the siting and building of data centers.
For example, in Florida, at least 20 counties and municipalities passed or discussed very strict guardrails on data centers.
In my home county, Hillsborough County, many say that is not the appropriate place for a data center because we don't have the water resources and we don't have the electricity yet to do that.
These are the wealthiest corporations in America.

sentences: I thank the gentleman for yielding and for his leadership on energy and clean air policy for all of America.
